item.title: Review: Look at Me by Dustin Hoffman review – an era-defining actor says his piece
item.description: At 89, the star of the Graduate and Ran Man demonstrates both brilliance and a startling lack of self-awareness The choice of title for an actor’s autobiography can be revealing. Sylvester Stallone went with The Steps , conflating life’s challenging progress with the grand staircase of the Philadelphia Museum of Art that Rocky euphorically ran up. Michael Douglas cheerfully and unreflectively called his One Helluva Ride. Dustin Hoffman’s is one of those that harks back to the poignantly vulnerable youthful world in which the acting bug first took effect. Al Pacino called his Sonny Boy ; Anthony Hopkins gave us We Did OK, Kid . Hoffman’s Look at Me is about the yearning to be seen and heard…

item.title: Review: Woeful Wallabies sink to new Twickenham low with no set-piece and no swagger | Gerard Meagher
item.description: Australia continue to struggle to find identity and a top-class fly-half a year before they host the World Cup On the shivering Twickenham concourses shortly after full time, one well-oiled Australia supporter took it upon himself to congratulate his forlorn compatriots for at least turning up. Alas, there were 15 of them conspicuous by their absence. Make no mistake, and take nothing away from England, but this was a woeful Wallabies performance, as bad as anything served up in recent memory – the kind that will shake executives to the core with a home World Cup tournament less than 12 months away. item.description: Man taken to hospital after falling off Royal Caribbean ship in Pacific Ocean, with Coast Guard investigating incident A pianist for a Royal Caribbean cruise ship is expected to survive after two Newport Beach, California , fishermen discovered him treading water in the Pacific Ocean nearly 20 miles (32km) offshore on Friday. item.title: Review: Dominant Lando Norris powers to victory in São Paulo F1 Grand Prix
item.description: Mercedes wrap up constructors’ championship Red Bull’s Max Verstappen surges to second place Lando Norris won the São Paulo Grand Prix after an incident-packed race at Interlagos, including a remarkable comeback for Max Verstappen who finished in second having started in 21st place. Kimi Antonelli, the newly crowned world champion, struggled with tyre problems to make it to fifth place but with his teammate George Russell fourth it was more than enough to ensure Mercedes sealed the Formula One constructors’ world championship.
